verses.1: Christ set us free for freedom. Stand firm then, and do not again submit to the yoke of slavery.
verses.2: Listen, I Paul say to you that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.
verses.3: I testify again to every person who is circumcised that he is obligated to do the whole law.
verses.4: You who are justified through the law have become estranged from Christ, and you have fallen away from grace.
verses.5: For we through the Spirit, by faith, eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness.
verses.6: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but faith working through love.
verses.7: You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth?
verses.8: That persuasion did not come from the one calling you.
verses.9: A little leaven leavens the whole batch.
verses.10: I am confident in the Lord that you will have no other mind. But the one disturbing you will bear his judgment, whoever he may be.
verses.11: But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the offense of the cross has been abolished.
verses.12: Let those who trouble you be cut off.
verses.13: For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but serve one another through love.
verses.14: For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.15: But if you bite and devour one another, watch that you are not consumed by one another.
verses.16: I say, walk in the Spirit, and you will not fulfill the desires of the flesh.
verses.17: For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. These are opposed to one another, so that you may not do what you want.
verses.18: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under law.
verses.19: Now the works of the flesh are plain, which are fornication, uncleanness, sensuality,
verses.20: idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, factions,
verses.21: envy, drunkenness, revelry, and the like, of which I say in advance, just as I said before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
verses.22: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
verses.23: gentleness, self-control. Against these there is no law.
verses.24: And those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
verses.25: If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.
verses.26: Let us not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness" — the Greek "περιπατεῖν" (to walk) is metaphorically rendered as "eagerly wait for" to reflect the dynamic expectation in the context of righteousness.
- v. 16: "you will not fulfill" — the Greek "τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν" is translated as "the desires" to avoid ambiguity about the subject of the fulfillment.
- v. 24: "have crucified the flesh" — the phrase is rendered as a past tense action, consistent with the aorist tense in the Greek, to emphasize the decisive nature of the action.
raw:
[1] Christ set us free for freedom. Stand firm then, and do not again submit to the yoke of slavery.

[2] Listen, I Paul say to you that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.

[3] I testify again to every person who is circumcised that he is obligated to do the whole law.

[4] You who are justified through the law have become estranged from Christ, and you have fallen away from grace.

[5] For we through the Spirit, by faith, eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness.

[6] For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but faith working through love.

[7] You were running well. Who hindered you from obeying the truth?

[8] That persuasion did not come from the one calling you.

[9] A little leaven leavens the whole batch.

[10] I am confident in the Lord that you will have no other mind. But the one disturbing you will bear his judgment, whoever he may be.

[11] But I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the offense of the cross has been abolished.

[12] Let those who trouble you be cut off.

[13] For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but serve one another through love.

[14] For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."

[15] But if you bite and devour one another, watch that you are not consumed by one another.

[16] I say, walk in the Spirit, and you will not fulfill the desires of the flesh.

[17] For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. These are opposed to one another, so that you may not do what you want.

[18] But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under law.

[19] Now the works of the flesh are plain, which are fornication, uncleanness, sensuality,

[20] idolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, divisions, factions,

[21] envy, drunkenness, revelry, and the like, of which I say in advance, just as I said before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.

[22] But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

[23] gentleness, self-control. Against these there is no law.

[24] And those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.

[25] If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.

[26] Let us not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.

Notes
- v. 13: "eagerly wait for the hope of righteousness" — the Greek "περιπατεῖν" (to walk) is metaphorically rendered as "eagerly wait for" to reflect the dynamic expectation in the context of righteousness.
- v. 16: "you will not fulfill" — the Greek "τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν" is translated as "the desires" to avoid ambiguity about the subject of the fulfillment.
- v. 24: "have crucified the flesh" — the phrase is rendered as a past tense action, consistent with the aorist tense in the Greek, to emphasize the decisive nature of the action.
